what: evidence that the graph face has been mounted in a real, non-headless window -- not only in the headless renderer tools/shoot.mjs and tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs drive
why: req/02 W15 clause 3: a face must carry proof of having mounted in a real window a person could look at. tools/browser-mount-smoke.mjs and tools/real-window-smoke.mjs in this same faces/graph/tools/ directory were written from zero for this face, following the same shape faces/ledger, faces/notice, faces/held and faces/receipt already established (fixture served over http + shell/tools/real_window.ps1, the shell's own real-window instrument, reused rather than duplicated).
how: tools/real-window-smoke.mjs starts a static file server rooted at the repo (answering /s-common/tokens.css from tokens/tokens.css, the one in-repo stylesheet of record), then shells out to shell/tools/real_window.ps1 with the fixture's URL. That script opens Chrome in app mode at 1440x900, waits, reads the window's own title back through the Win32 window list, and screenshots the on-screen window rectangle. This face's mount fixture (fixtures/browser-mount-entry.mjs + fixtures/browser-mount.html) imports index.mjs directly and calls mount(host, stubPort, []) against a folded list envelope of four transformations spelled out inline in the fixture -- two paths, one a genuine in-window chain (deck.pdf) and one carrying an edge that leaves the window (budget.xlsx, whose first touch names a predecessor 't-900' this window never read). The entry script writes the element/group counts into document.title so the numbers below are the numbers the page itself computed, not typed by hand.
